title: quant-runtime: unexpected op-level fallback spike causing canary instability and capacity contention
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Production canary for quantized LLM models experienced a rapid rise in operator-level fallbacks from optimized INT8 kernels to a generic slower path. The fallback spike increased per-request CPU time, triggered autoscaler oscillations, and led to degraded latency and several canary crash loops. This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations, and follow-up action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-24 02:13 UTC - Canary fleet alert: 3x increase in p95 generation latency for quantized model profile 'redwood-llama-13b-q8'
2026-02-24 02:14 UTC - Runtime observed rising counts of op_fallback events in metrics (fused_conv_transpose + channelwise_mul)
2026-02-24 02:18 UTC - Canary autoscaler triggered scale-up; new nodes failed to reach ready state due to CPU saturation during kernel fallbacks
2026-02-24 02:27 UTC - Two canary VMs entered crashloop backoff after repeated generic-op exceptions; automated rollback to float model variant initiated
2026-02-24 02:35 UTC - On-call routed to quant-runtime on-call and infra on-call for capacity stabilization
investigation_notes: Observed that fallback rate correlated with specific sequences of token lengths and dynamic shapes that were underrepresented in canary sampling.

Trace logs show op signature mismatch between converter-generated op map and runtime kernel registry for fused_conv_transpose when input channel stride == 3, causing runtime to mark kernel unusable and call into a slower generic implementation.
Reproducer created using a scripted prompt set; deterministic on local repro with same tokenization and batch shape sampling (see attachment link to repro notebook).
No model weight corruption detected; issue is behavioral/compatibility between converter op fingerprint and selected INT8 kernel's supported shape set.
Autoscaler oscillation exacerbated the problem: scale-up added nodes under load which caused increased retry rates and API timeouts, leading to crashloop symptoms for the canary group.
root_cause: A shape-coverage gap in our INT8 kernel capability table combined with an opsig (operator signature) mapping drift in the quant converter. The converter emitted operator metadata that matched a deprecated fused operator name; runtime failed kernel compatibility checks for a narrow set of input strides and fell back to a slow generic path. Canary sampling did not include those stride cases, so the regression surfaced only in load with real traffic patterns.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back canary to float (non-quant) variant at 2026-02-24 02:27 UTC to restore latency SLOs.
Pinned kernel compatibility table to last-known-good version and disabled the new converter deployment until patch landed.
Applied temporary throttle on canary traffic and disabled aggressive autoscale policy for quantized pool to prevent oscillation.
Notified downstream customers on Dedicated alpha cohorts — advisory issued via status channel.
action_items: AI-1: Patch converter to include opsig aliasing table so deprecated fused names map correctly to current kernel registry (owner: Marco Santoro, estimate 3) - target runtime-2.3.1-hotfix.
AI-2: Extend kernel capability matrix to include dynamic strides sampling and add unit tests for channel strides 1..8 (owner: Linh Tran, estimate 5).

AI-3: Improve canary sampling harness to include production-like dynamic shape distributions and token length tails; add 10k synthetic examples derived from production traces (owner: SRE team, estimate 3).
AI-4: Add runtime metric alert for op_fallback_rate with absolute and relative thresholds (owner: Observability team, estimate 2).
AI-5: Harden autoscaler safety: introduce cooldown and bounded concurrency per-pool to avoid scale oscillation during sudden per-request CPU spikes (owner: Infra-autoscale, estimate 5).
AI-6: Create deterministic regression test that exercises the reproduced sequence and run it in CI for converter + runtime integration (owner: QA, estimate 2).
AI-7: Schedule a short post-deployment canary soak window (72h) for future quant-related releases and require explicit sign-off from Quant Stability SIG (owner: Release Eng, estimate 1).
followups: Validate patched converter on internal benchmark harness against 3 representative models (7B, 13B, 70B) and report token-level latency and fallback counts.
Roll out runtime-2.3.1-hotfix to canary pool with 5% traffic for 72h with enhanced op_fallback monitoring.
Coordinate with Product to update customer-facing runbook for quant regressions and add guidance for pinning model variants.
Document incident and add to reliability playbooks; present retrospective at weekly SRE forum.
